title: Maha Shivaratri: the great night of Shiva
hook: a night kept awake, water poured over the lingam, Om Namah Shivaya until dawn
tomorrow: karma — the Isha Upanishad as a life

segments.voice: Yesterday: Holi, Narasimha from the pillar, and Prahlad asking for his father's release. Everyone's the same color today.

Two gods are arguing about which of them is greater: Brahma, the creator, and Vishnu, the preserver. It's getting heated. Then, between them, a column of fire appears, with no visible top and no visible bottom. It just goes up and down, beyond seeing. The argument stops. This is one of the best-known stories told about why the lingam is worshiped, and why some people keep Shivaratri awake all night.
screen: `BRAHMA AND VISHNU ARGUE.` → `A COLUMN OF FIRE APPEARS.` → `NO TOP, NO BOTTOM.`

segments.voice: The story is told in the Shiva Purana and other Puranas, and it's called the Lingodbhava, the appearance of the lingam. The two gods agree: whoever finds an end of the pillar is the greater. Vishnu becomes a boar and digs downward. Brahma becomes a swan and flies upward. They go for ages, and neither finds an end. Vishnu comes back and says honestly: I couldn't find it. Brahma, in many tellings, claims he did, and is caught in the lie. Then Shiva appears from inside the pillar of fire, and the argument about who's greatest ends with both bowing to something with no edges at all. Many Shaivas say Maha Shivaratri is the night that pillar appeared. That changes how the lingam looks: not a statue of a face, but a sign, a mark, of what can't be measured in either direction. So on Shivaratri the night is divided into four watches, called praharas, roughly three hours each. In many temples and homes there's an abhisheka in each watch, the lingam bathed again, often with a different offering each time: milk, curd, ghee, honey, and always water. In between, the five syllables: na, mah, shi, va, ya. Om Namah Shivaya. And with that, the festival weeks are done: twenty days of lamps and colors and threads and cradles and clay and nine nights. Tomorrow the lineage track begins, with the path of action and a short Upanishad read as a whole life.
screen: `LINGODBHAVA: THE PILLAR OF FIRE.` · `NEITHER GOD FINDS AN END.` · `A SIGN OF WHAT CAN'T BE MEASURED.` · `FOUR WATCHES, FOUR BATHS.` · then, large: `STAY AWAKE FOR WHAT MATTERS.`

segments.voice: Follow one breath all the way in, looking for where it begins, then all the way out, looking for where it ends. You may not find either edge, the way neither god found the pillar's end, and that's fine. When you want to stop, stay three breaths longer, just watching.
Shivaratri. The great night of Shiva, kept in four watches, and remembered by many as the night the pillar of fire appeared, with no end either way.
Your line: stay awake for what matters. Some things have no edge to find. Day six hundred eighty-nine, done.

screen: `DAY 689 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: KARMA — THE ISHA UPANISHAD AS A LIFE.`

howItsDone: On Maha Shivaratri many Shiva temples and households divide the night into four watches and bathe the lingam in each, with water, milk, curd, ghee or honey, chanting Om Namah Shivaya until dawn; Lingodbhava images often appear on the western wall of South Indian Shiva temples.

original.note: Sanskrit liṅga (sign, mark) + udbhava (appearance, arising): the lingam's appearance as a pillar of fire.

trapdoor: what you thought: the lingam is a statue of Shiva.
what it means: it's a sign, recalling the pillar of fire with no end above or below.
what a scholar hears: liṅga means sign or mark; the Lingodbhava story appears in the Shiva, Linga and other Puranas, and is carved on many South Indian temple walls.

chat.says: Why is the Shiva lingam shaped like a column instead of a face?
options: In one well-known story, it's a pillar of fire with no end, beyond measuring.
It marks the spot where Brahma found the top of the pillar of fire.
It's a statue of the tree Shiva sat under while he meditated.
chat.meaning: In the Lingodbhava, neither Brahma nor Vishnu finds the pillar's end; the lingam is a sign of what can't be measured either way.
